_schema: life_bank — Axis B (all aspects of life). APPEND-only across sessions.

concepts.name: Cheese affinage (ripeness judged by touch)
concepts.open_problem: An affineur decides when a wheel of cheese is at peak maturity by pressing it with the fingertips and using accumulated sensory instinct; there is no objective, non-destructive instrument that predicts optimal ripeness per-wheel, so timing-to-market is done by feel.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The skilled affineur will need to use their finely-tuned senses (alongside a grading iron) to ascertain the cheese's stage of maturity and make decisions as to whether the cheese is ready for market.

concepts.name: Koji (Aspergillus) cultivation timing by smell/feel
concepts.open_problem: Koji makers judge when mold growth on rice/beans is finished by looking at the mycelia and smelling/tasting for a fruity-floral note; this finicky tacit skill is passed hand-to-hand and has no reliable in-tray sensor for end-point detection.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Sake craftspeople oversee the process to ensure the mould grows in optimal conditions by adjusting temperature and humidity, and their work determines the quality of the sake.

concepts.name: Soy sauce / miso moromi maturity assessment
concepts.open_problem: Maturity of the moromi (fermenting mash) over 6-18+ months is still gauged by an experienced brewer's nose and eye; the literature itself notes the lack of any objective, fast, intuitive maturity metric.
concepts.verbatim_quote: there is currently a deficiency of an objective, fast, and intuitive evaluation method for maturity.

concepts.name: Dry-cured ham testing by the 'cala' (bone-needle smell test)
concepts.open_problem: Whether a 24-36 month jamon is correctly cured is verified by a 'calador' who pierces the ham at four points with a bone spike and judges the released aroma; the entire quality gate depends on one expert's trained sense of smell with no instrument substitute.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The 'cala' is a very complex process and it is necessary to have an excellent and highly developed sense of smell developed through experience.

concepts.name: Sourdough bulk-fermentation / proof end-point ('poke test')
concepts.open_problem: Bakers ignore the clock and decide dough is proofed by how it looks and springs back to a finger poke; end-point depends on temperature and starter vigor and is learned by watching the dough, with no consumer-accessible objective readiness signal.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Use time as a guideline, but let the dough tell you when it's ready.

concepts.name: Wine harvest timing (post-veraison ripeness call)
concepts.open_problem: The pick date 30-70 days after veraison is a judgment blending lab Brix/pH with tasting seeds and skins; picking a day early or late shifts the wine, and the final call remains a stylistic sensory decision.
concepts.verbatim_quote: harvest typically follows 30 to 70 days after véraison, depending on variety, climate, and the winemaker's stylistic goals.

concepts.name: Traditional balsamic vinegar barrel maturation
concepts.open_problem: Over 12-25 years of annual barrel transfers in an acetaia, the maestro decides which barrel/vintage is ready purely by tasting; each acetaia's progression is idiosyncratic and assessment is by master palate, not measurement.
concepts.verbatim_quote: As master tasters know well, each balsamic vinegar is unique and releases an inimitable range of flavours and aromatic notes.

concepts.name: Blacksmithing / forge welding heat judged by color
concepts.open_problem: Smiths bring steel to forge-welding heat by reading the incandescent color of the metal by eye; the exact temperature is judged visually and learned per-forge, complicated by ambient light, with no affordable real-time guidance.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The exact temperature is almost always judged by eye and learned by experience on your set of equipment.

concepts.name: Pottery kiln firing without instruments
concepts.open_problem: Traditional potters control temperature, soak time and oxidation/reduction atmosphere by reading flame color, ember glow and the look of the pots; this is instinctive expert knowledge with no low-cost sensing of in-kiln atmosphere/temperature for the artisan.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Without pyrometers or electric kilns, traditional potters relied on the color of the flames, the glowing embers, and the appearance of the pots themselves to gauge temperature, duration, and atmosphere parameters.

concepts.name: Glassblowing (working glass at the right viscosity by eye)
concepts.open_problem: A gaffer keeps molten glass in the narrow workable viscosity band by reading its color (e.g. bright orange near 1090 C) and feel, knowing when to reheat; it is kinesthetic memory built over years with no instrument feeding the working state in real time.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The working temperature is reduced in the furnace to around 1,090 °C (2,000 °F), at which stage the glass appears to be a bright orange color.

concepts.name: Handloom weaving warp-tension management by feel
concepts.open_problem: On traditional shuttle looms the weaver continuously feels warp tension, reads the cloth and adjusts by hand for hours; even tension across hundreds of threads is maintained purely by tactile judgment with no assistive feedback.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Traditional shuttle looms depend entirely on human judgment, and they require a weaver who can feel the tension, read the cloth, and respond to the material as it behaves under their hands.

concepts.name: Dry stone walling (stone selection and fit by eye)
concepts.open_problem: A mortarless wall stands only by gravity, friction and the waller's eye for which irregular stone to place where; certification is a timed hands-on rebuild, and stone selection/placement is an un-tooled spatial-reasoning skill judged by experts.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Dry stone walling is so durable because it contains no mortar to crack and fail, but is held together merely by the weight of stone, and by the skill of the builder who selected and fitted the stones together.

concepts.name: Japanese kumiko / nail-free joinery fitting
concepts.open_problem: Kumiko pieces hold together by pressure alone, requiring each thin slat to be planed, sawn and chiseled to a hand-fitted tolerance; achieving the exact interference fit is a by-hand fine-adjustment skill with no digital aid for the artisan.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Thinly-slit wooden pieces are grooved, punched, and mortised, and then fitted individually using a plane, saw, chisel, and other tools to make fine-adjustments.

concepts.name: Vegetable tanning of leather (recipe and feel by master tanner)
concepts.open_problem: A master tanner sets tannin sources, concentrations, temperatures and weeks-to-months timings by judgment to hit a target softness/strength/touch; recipes are secret, hide-by-hide, and tuned by feel rather than by a predictive model.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The master tanner creates the ideal blend keeping in mind the result he wants to achieve in terms of softness, strength, colour and touch feeling.

concepts.name: Apiculture queen detection / hive inspection
concepts.open_problem: Beekeepers must manually open hives and inspect frames to confirm the queen is present and laying; her loss can collapse a colony, but inspection is intrusive, time-consuming, weather-limited, and depends on the beekeeper's eye for spotting a single bee or fresh eggs among thousands.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Manual inspections are laborious and disruptive, motivating the need for automated, non-invasive detection methods.

concepts.name: Varroa mite monitoring (alcohol wash / sugar roll)
concepts.open_problem: To decide whether to treat for varroa, beekeepers take a ~300-bee sample, dislodge mites with alcohol or powdered sugar, and count mites by hand against seasonal thresholds; counting is tedious, error-prone, kills the sample (alcohol), and is done by feel/eye rather than any automated sensor.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The powdered sugar roll is currently the most common and quickest tool to monitor mites.

concepts.name: Sericulture cocoon grading and silk reeling
concepts.open_problem: Silk quality depends on grading cocoons and reeling filament from them, traditionally judged by experienced workers by eye/feel (shell ratio, defects, seasonal quality); the larva must be killed at the chrysalis stage before the moth breaks the filament, and grading remains a hands-on craft.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Because an emerging moth would break the cocoon filament, the larva is killed in the cocoon by steam or hot air at the chrysalis stage.

concepts.name: Orphan / underutilized crop breeding
concepts.open_problem: Neglected crops vital to smallholders (e.g. fonio, bambara groundnut, teff) have almost no genomic or breeding resources and little institutional data; improvement is done with minimal investment and lost institutional memory, far behind wheat/rice/maize.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Orphan crops are also known as underutilized crops, neglected crops or crops for the future, named for the lack of genetic improvement, not for lack of use or incorporation into cultural diets.

concepts.name: Agroforestry / alley cropping design
concepts.open_problem: Designing tree-crop alley systems requires predicting decades of light/water/nutrient competition between rows of trees and alley crops, but interactions are poorly characterized and the long time horizon means design is largely by rule-of-thumb and farmer judgment.
concepts.verbatim_quote: As trees and shrubs grow, they influence light, water and nutrient regimes in the field, and these interactions are what sets alley cropping apart from more common monocropping systems.

concepts.name: Seed saving: roguing and isolation
concepts.open_problem: Keeping a landrace/heirloom variety true-to-type requires the saver to recognize and remove off-type plants (roguing) before pollination and to maintain isolation distances; this is judgment-by-eye over whole populations with essentially no decision-support tooling.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Roguing is the process of removing weak or "off-type" plants before they spread their pollen.

concepts.name: Soil judging / field texture-by-feel
concepts.open_problem: Classifying a soil in the field (texture, clay/sand percentage, horizons) is done by hand-feel ribboning and color books in a pit, a tacit skill built by practice; there is no portable instrument that replaces the trained fingers used in soil/land judging.
concepts.verbatim_quote: In the field, it is necessary to estimate the soil texture by feeling it with the fingers, a skill that can be developed with practice and will be used in contests.

concepts.name: Polynesian wayfinding (star compass & wave piloting)
concepts.open_problem: Traditional navigators cross open Pacific ocean with no instruments, holding course by a memorized 32-house star compass and reading swell patterns/refraction off islands entirely in the head; the knowledge is oral, hard to teach, and has no computational model.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The star compass is a mental construct and not physical like a western compass.

concepts.name: Inuit snow/wind (sastrugi) wayfinding
concepts.open_problem: Arctic travelers orient in whiteouts and on featureless sea ice by reading wind-carved snow ridges (sastrugi), named prevailing winds, ice sounds, and animal cues; this is a multi-sensory tacit skill with no GPS-independent tooling that captures it.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The snowdrifts left by prevailing winds are the most reliable source of spatial orientation, and only the drifts left by prevailing winds can last throughout the winter.

concepts.name: Maritime pilotage (local-knowledge ship handling)
concepts.open_problem: Harbour/river pilots con large ships through dangerous waterways using visual references and intimate local knowledge of tides, currents, silting and shoals not shown on charts; this expertise is tacit, firsthand, and resists codification.
concepts.verbatim_quote: A maritime pilot is a mariner who has specific knowledge of an often dangerous or congested waterway, such as harbors or river mouths.

concepts.name: Orienteering route choice / map-terrain matching
concepts.open_problem: Orienteers must continuously match a topographic map to terrain while moving at speed and choose among routes weighing distance, climb, vegetation and footing; route choice and proactive map-reading are cognitive skills with little algorithmic support for the runner.
concepts.verbatim_quote: A handrail is defined as a linear feature on a map that parallels your route and can be used as a quick aid to navigating yourself to the next control.

concepts.name: Cave navigation & survey (compass/clinometer/tape)
concepts.open_problem: Underground there is no GPS and no map until someone makes one; cavers find their way and build surveys leg-by-leg with magnetic compass, clinometer and tape, fighting magnetic interference, reading error and slowness, often relying on a guideline to find the way out.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The DistoX2 unit is a beefed-up laser rangefinder used to measure the distance and direction between survey stations underground.

concepts.name: Dead reckoning (manual position keeping)
concepts.open_problem: When fixes are unavailable, navigators advance a known position by hand from logged speed, heading and time; errors accumulate (~10-15% of distance) until a fix lets them reinitialize, and the running plot is maintained manually by the navigator's feel.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The errors that are inherent in dead reckoning accumulate; when a position has been checked, the reckoning is therefore generally restarted from that position.

concepts.name: Desert wayfinding (Tuareg/Bedouin dune navigation)
concepts.open_problem: Desert nomads cross shifting sand seas by recognizing slow-moving dune systems, named dunes, rock formations, sun and stars, with routes and dune names taught orally; the landscape changes with wind and the skill lives only in inherited memory.
concepts.verbatim_quote: While the wind in the desert is constantly changing the landscape, the big dune systems are moving very slowly, so they are more recognizable and can be used as landmarks.

concepts.name: Whistled language interpretation (Silbo Gomero)
concepts.open_problem: Whistled registers like Silbo Gomero compress a full spoken language into a tiny set of pitch/continuity contrasts (only ~2-4 whistled vowels and 4-10 consonants), and decoding them back into speech is done entirely by trained human ears in real time; there is no robust tool to transcribe or translate whistled speech, and the practice survives in only a handful of communities worldwide.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Silbo replaces each vowel or consonant with a whistling sound.

concepts.name: Sign language transcription and glossing (no standard notation)
concepts.open_problem: Signed languages have no commonly accepted written or transcription system, so linguists hand-gloss video utterance-by-utterance using ad hoc systems (Stokoe, HamNoSys, glosses); annotation is slow, inconsistent across labs, and there is no widely usable automatic notation/transcription pipeline for the spatial-simultaneous structure of signs.
concepts.verbatim_quote: There is no commonly accepted transcription system for describing the form of signs.

concepts.name: Prosody and intonation labeling (ToBI)
concepts.open_problem: Labeling the intonation/prosody of speech with the standard ToBI system is extraordinarily slow expert manual work (roughly 100-200x real time per minute of audio) and even trained labelers achieve only moderate inter-transcriber agreement, leaving most speech corpora unannotated for prosody.
concepts.verbatim_quote: A ToBI prosodic labeling of speech typically takes even experienced labelers from 100 to 200 times real time.

concepts.name: Tone-language transcription in phonetic fieldwork
concepts.open_problem: Documenting the tone systems of under-described African and Asian languages relies on manually marking pitch height and contour (e.g. numeric 1-5 notation) by ear; transcribers need months of specialised training, the work is slow and costly, and it is racing against the rapid disappearance of endangered tone languages.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Current phonetic fieldwork relies on manual effort, resulting in substantial time and financial costs, especially challenging for endangered languages that are rapidly disappearing with limited funding.

concepts.name: Dialectology fieldwork and linguistic-atlas compilation
concepts.open_problem: Traditional dialect mapping still depends on painstaking in-person fieldwork (questionnaires, hand phonetic transcription, isogloss drawing) targeting specific NORM speakers; compiling a linguistic atlas is slow, expensive and labour-intensive, so most regions and dialect continua remain only partially surveyed.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The preparation and compilation of linguistic atlases is a difficult, costly, voluminous, and time-consuming job.

concepts.name: Cuneiform tablet reading backlog (Assyriology)
concepts.open_problem: Of the hundreds of thousands of excavated cuneiform tablets, the large majority have never been read or published because transliteration requires years of training and only a few hundred qualified experts exist worldwide; the script has no word spacing and signs are polyvalent, making automated reading still nascent and unreliable.
concepts.verbatim_quote: An estimated half a million tablets are held in museums across the world, but comparatively few of these are published.

concepts.name: Historical linguistic reconstruction via the comparative method
concepts.open_problem: Reconstructing proto-languages is done by hand: linguists identify cognate sets, line up sound correspondences, and propose proto-forms following phonetic rules; this is slow expert judgement work with little tooling, and it breaks down beyond ~8,000-10,000 years as cognates become unrecognisable.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Reconstruction becomes unreliable beyond roughly 8,000 to 10,000 years, as sound changes accumulate to the point where cognates are no longer recognizable.

concepts.name: Snakebite responsible-species identification
concepts.open_problem: Choosing the right antivenom depends on knowing which snake bit the patient, but the snake is rarely seen, victim descriptions are misleading, and frontline rural hospital staff are usually not trained to identify the biting species even when it is brought in dead - so antivenom choice is often guesswork in exactly the low-resource settings where snakebite kills most.
concepts.verbatim_quote: In many cases of envenoming following snake bite, the snake responsible for the accident remains unidentified; this frequently results in difficulty deciding which antivenom to administer to the systemically-envenomed victim, especially when only monospecific antivenoms are available.

concepts.name: Chronic wound assessment (visual and manual measurement)
concepts.open_problem: Tracking whether a chronic wound is healing relies on a clinician's naked-eye judgement of size and tissue type plus manual ruler measurement; this is highly subjective, varies with the clinician's experience, and manual area estimates can deviate enormously (up to 40-75%) from true wound size, with poor inter-rater reliability.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Wound assessment and measurement depend on visual examination, which can be highly subjective and dependent on the clinician's experience.

concepts.name: Ethnobotanical / traditional herbal medicine knowledge documentation
concepts.open_problem: Vast bodies of traditional herbal-remedy knowledge held by healers are undocumented and passed only by word of mouth; with the spread of modern medicine this knowledge is being eroded and lost generation by generation, and capturing it depends on slow manual ethnobotanical surveys.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Most cultures possess a huge store of undocumented traditional knowledge of applying herbal remedies in the treatment of diseases.

concepts.name: Ethnoveterinary medicine documentation and dosing
concepts.open_problem: Smallholder farmers across Africa and Asia treat livestock with plant-based home remedies where vets are unavailable, but the practice suffers from poor knowledge of application rates/dosage, inadequate diagnosis, and almost no documentation or standardisation - an indigenous knowledge system with essentially no decision-support tooling.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Some farmers have failed to use ethnoveterinary medicine due to poor knowledge of application rates (dosage), inadequate diagnosis, lack of documentation and side effects of the concoctions.

concepts.name: Prosthetic socket fitting (craft skill)
concepts.open_problem: Getting a comfortable prosthetic socket fit is a hand craft: the prosthetist casts the residual limb, manually 'rectifies' the positive mould, and iterates check sockets by feel; the result is time-consuming, expensive and heavily dependent on the individual prosthetist's skill, with little objective guidance on where to add or relieve pressure.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The process is time-consuming expensive and heavily dependent on the individual skills of the prosthetist.

concepts.name: Observational gait analysis in clinic
concepts.open_problem: Most clinical gait assessment is done by a therapist watching the patient walk and visually estimating joint angles and step parameters with no instrumentation; reliability is poor, results depend on the evaluator's expertise, and inter-rater agreement is low - yet instrumented labs are rarely available, so the subjective method dominates practice.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Reliability of observational analysis is poor, and therapists should be encouraged to use objective measures to give a more representative account of the gait pattern.

concepts.name: Partograph-based labour monitoring in low-resource midwifery
concepts.open_problem: In low-resource maternity settings the partograph (manual plotting of cervical dilatation and fetal/maternal signs against alert/action lines) is the main tool to catch obstructed or abnormal labour, but correct use is labour-intensive, completion rates are low, and there are too few skilled attendants - so warning signs are missed where maternal/newborn mortality is highest.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The correct and effective use of the partograph is labour intensive even with the requisite skills, making it unfriendly to use in situations where the delivery rates are high with few skilled attendants.

concepts.name: Lutherie and tonewood selection
concepts.open_problem: Selecting a specific piece of tonewood (spruce/maple billet) for a violin and predicting its acoustic outcome is done by expert feel — tapping, flexing, eyeing grain — because the internal structure of wood is uncertain and only roughly one tree in a thousand meets professional criteria. There is no tooling that maps a raw billet's measurable physical properties to the finished instrument's sound, so makers rely on tacit, hard-to-transfer judgment.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The craft of luthiers, lutherie, is commonly divided into the two main categories of makers of stringed instruments that are plucked or strummed and makers of stringed instruments that are bowed.

concepts.name: Change ringing method composition (campanology)
concepts.open_problem: Composing a 'peal' or 'touch' requires arranging thousands of bell-order permutations so that no row repeats ('truth') while remaining musical and physically ringable, and the conductor must memorise the entire composition. This combinatorial design over factorial-sized permutation groups is still done largely by hand and by tradition by a small community of expert conductors/composers.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Change ringing is the art of ringing a set of tuned bells in a tightly controlled manner to produce precise variations in their successive striking sequences, known as "changes".

concepts.name: Inpainting / retouching in painting conservation
concepts.open_problem: Filling losses (lacunae) in a damaged painting so the fill blends with surrounding colours but does not cover any original paint, while staying reversible and ethically distinguishable, is an extremely time-consuming hand process driven by case-by-case expert judgement and contested philosophy. Generative image inpainting exists for photos but is essentially unused for physical conservation decisions, colour-matching aged varnish, or reversibility constraints.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Inpainting is the work done by a conservator-restorer to reinstate obliterated or damaged areas in a pictorial layer, in a way that blends with the surrounding colors but without covering any of the original paint.

concepts.name: Stained glass conservation and matching antique glass
concepts.open_problem: When restoring a historic window, matching replacement glass to the original colour depth, texture, seeds (bubbles) and light behaviour is the most technically demanding and visually critical step; conservators do it by eye, sometimes plating two layers (one for colour, one for texture) so the patch does not read as a patch. There is no computational tool to predict perceived match under varying transmitted light or to recommend a plating recipe.
concepts.verbatim_quote: When matching colored textured glass is not available, it is possible to use two layers of glass, one for texture and one for color, rather than installing a poorly matched piece that would be visible.

concepts.name: Labanotation / dance notation transcription
concepts.open_problem: Transcribing live or recorded human movement into a Labanotation score (direction, level, body part, duration, dynamics) is difficult, time-consuming and depends on a shrinking pool of trained notators; not all expressive movement maps cleanly to symbols. Automatic, accurate motion-to-Labanotation generation remains an open, barely-served problem, leaving most of the world's choreography unrecorded.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Labanotation is a system for analyzing and recording human movement, invented by Austro-Hungarian choreographer and dancer Rudolf von Laban (1879–1958).

concepts.name: Tuvan throat singing / overtone singing technique
concepts.open_problem: Throat singers produce two simultaneous pitches by precisely shaping the vocal tract to focus a single overtone above a sustained drone; mastering and teaching styles like khoomei, sygyt and kargyraa is done by ear and imitation. There is essentially no real-time pedagogical tool that analyses a learner's overtone focusing and gives corrective feedback on tongue/pharynx shaping.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Khoomei is traditionally a softer sounding style, with the fundamental (or drone) usually in the low-mid to midrange of the singer's normal voice.

concepts.name: Traditional lake pigment making
concepts.open_problem: Producing historical lake pigments (e.g. madder, carmine) by precipitating a natural dye onto a mordant is a centuries-old recipe craft whose colour, lightfastness and transparency depend on subtle, poorly-documented control of pH, mordant ratio and source material. Reconstructing or optimising these recipes for conservation/reproduction is done by trial-and-error by a handful of specialists.
concepts.verbatim_quote: A lake pigment is a pigment made by precipitating a dye with an inert binder, or mordant, usually a metallic salt.

concepts.name: Marionette manipulation (string puppetry)
concepts.open_problem: Animating a marionette convincingly through many strings (Burmese yoke thé use 18–19 wires) is a dexterous expert skill, hardest when there is no central control rod; transmission of this craft is endangered. There is little to no tooling for capturing, notating, or assisting marionette manipulation, or for mapping desired character motion to per-string control.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Burmese marionettes are very intricate and their use requires dexterous skills, employing 18 or 19 wires for male and female characters respectively, with each puppet controlled by only one puppeteer.

concepts.name: Gift economy and obligations of reciprocity
concepts.open_problem: In gift economies the obligations to give, receive and reciprocate (Mauss) govern social standing, yet deciding the appropriate counter-gift, timing and value to maintain honour is tacit cultural knowledge. There is no formal/computational modelling tool used by communities to reason about reciprocity obligations, debt of honour, or fairness in gift exchange networks.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Because of the bond between giver and gift, the act of giving creates a social bond with an obligation to reciprocate on the part of the recipient.

concepts.name: Computus (calculation of the date of Easter)
concepts.open_problem: Computus is the traditional algorithmic determination of moveable feast dates from ecclesiastical lunar/solar cycles (golden number, epact, Sunday letter). Reconciling competing historical computistical systems, reconstructing dates in fragmentary medieval calendars, and resolving Julian/Gregorian and Eastern/Western divergences is specialist manual scholarship with little modern tooling beyond fixed formulas.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Easter is the Sunday following the Paschal full moon date, which is the ecclesiastical full moon date on or after the ecclesiastical equinox on 21 March.

concepts.name: Divination and interpretation of signs/omens
concepts.open_problem: Across hundreds of divination systems (haruspicy, augury, scrying, casting lots) the practitioner's core task is interpreting effectively random or natural phenomena into meaningful guidance for a querent within a ritual frame. This interpretive act is purely human/traditional; the under-served angle is formalising and comparing the symbolic interpretation systems themselves, not predicting the future.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Divination is the attempt to gain insight into a question or situation by way of a magic ritual or practice.

concepts.name: Barter and the double coincidence of wants
concepts.open_problem: Pure barter requires a double coincidence of wants — each party must want exactly what the other holds at the same time and place — which is improbable and historically limits moneyless trade. In modern barter rings, swap meets and sharing/gift networks, finding multi-party trade cycles that satisfy everyone is done informally; there is little practical matching tooling for community-scale non-monetary exchange.
concepts.verbatim_quote: The coincidence of wants (often known as double coincidence of wants) is an economic phenomenon where two parties each hold an item that the other wants, so they exchange these items directly.

concepts.name: Funerary / mortuary customs
concepts.open_problem: Mortuary customs (interment, excarnation, heart-burial, grave goods, mourning rites) are a vast, culturally-specific complex of beliefs and practices, much of it undocumented and endangered. Systematically recording, comparing and reconstructing variation in death rituals across cultures (and matching archaeological remains to likely practices) is manual ethnographic/archaeological work.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Funerary customs comprise the complex of beliefs and practices used by a culture to remember and respect the dead, from interment, to various monuments, prayers, and rituals undertaken in their honour.

concepts.name: Mechanical watch regulation (horology)
concepts.open_problem: Regulating a mechanical movement — adjusting the escapement and balance so the watch keeps time across positions, temperatures and states of wind — requires cleaning, lubrication and calibration by a skilled watchmaker working by feel and timegrapher traces. Diagnosing rate errors and prescribing adjustments remains an expert manual craft with little assistive intelligence.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Mechanical watches are typically not as accurate as quartz watches, and they eventually require periodic cleaning, lubrication and calibration by a skilled watchmaker.

concepts.name: Kinship terminology systems analysis
concepts.open_problem: Different cultures encode relatives with structured kin-term systems whose generative logic (how terms compose to compute any relation) is an algebraic structure that anthropologists currently derive largely by hand. Eliciting, formalising and comparing these terminologies across the world's languages is labour-intensive and under-tooled despite being amenable to computation.
concepts.verbatim_quote: During the 1950s and '60s, the formal analysis of systems of classification on the basis of their different component distinctions within a semantic domain became known as "componential analysis."

concepts.name: Go scoring and life-and-death / seki determination
concepts.open_problem: Settling a Go game requires agreeing which groups are alive or dead and resolving ambiguous positions such as seki, where neither player can play without being captured — a judgement amateurs frequently dispute and that traditional scoring leaves to consensus. While top engines play superbly, accessible, explainable tools that adjudicate disputed life-and-death/seki and teach the reasoning to beginners are largely missing.
concepts.verbatim_quote: Another important concept is seki, a situation in which neither player can play on a particular point without then allowing the other player to play at another point to capture.

concepts.name: Judging forging heat by color (red heat)
concepts.open_problem: Smiths read the incandescent glow color (dull red -> orange -> yellow -> white) to judge a workpiece's temperature and workability by eye, with no instrument; tacit because the right color depends on alloy, ambient light, and the specific operation, and is the gatekeeper for every forging/welding decision.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (searched forge/heat-treatment color apps; only static color charts and educational PDFs returned, no shipping app that reads steel color via camera for a smith)
concepts.verbatim_quote: In blacksmithing, red heat is the practice of using colours to determine the temperature of a piece of metal (usually iron or steel).

concepts.name: Watching temper colors 'run' (oxide-color tempering)
concepts.open_problem: After hardening, the smith draws temper by watching a thin oxide film change color (straw -> brown -> purple -> blue) and quenching the instant the target color reaches the edge; the entire window is only ~400-700F with a few degrees per color, so the judgment is fast, lighting-dependent, and very hard to quantify.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (only LightSpectrum Pro, an unrelated film color-temperature app, surfaced; no app detects steel temper-color run)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Heat colors develop in a narrow 400ºF to 700ºF temperature range with only a few degrees separating each color, making it difficult to stop heating at the desired color.

concepts.name: Forge-weld timing and temperature window
concepts.open_problem: A sound forge weld depends on hitting a narrow near-white welding heat and on flux/hammer timing: too cool and it will not bond, too hot and it sparks/burns and the weld is brittle. The smith judges the exact moment to flux, withdraw, and strike almost entirely by eye and feel.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (searched forge-welding apps; only guides, forums, and color charts, no tool that times/judges the weld)
concepts.verbatim_quote: care must be taken to avoid overheating the metal to the point that it gives off sparks from rapid oxidation (burning), or else the weld will be poor and brittle.

concepts.name: Quench judgment / interrupted (mar-)quench
concepts.open_problem: Choosing quenchant and reading the quench in real time (the hiss/spit, when to pull the part during an interrupted quench so it stops cooling around 400-500F) to harden without cracking; described as an art reflecting the smith's experience rather than a measured procedure.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (results were technique blogs and quenching sound-effect clips, no shipping product that guides/monitors a quench)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The interrupted quench is an improvised version of what industry calls mar-quenching.

concepts.name: Bloomery smelter decision-making (judging the bloom)
concepts.open_problem: In bloomery iron smelting the smelter continuously judges airflow, charge rate, ore-charcoal ratio, residence time, and slag condition by sensory cues to grow a good bloom and know when it is ready; this tacit decision-making directly determines the product but is not captured in any model for the traditional process.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (ML exists for MODERN industrial blast/ladle furnaces, but no consumer or hobbyist tool for traditional bloomery decision-making)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The decisions include airflow and charging rate, temperature, residence time in the reducing zone, ore-charcoal ratio, and control of slag characteristics, with results demonstrating the direct impact of these decisions during bloomery smelting.

concepts.name: Reading slag and tap-hole management
concepts.open_problem: Operators judge furnace condition from the slag's flow, color, viscosity, and the look of what comes out of the tap-hole, deciding when and how to tap; slag carries the signatures of furnace conditions yet 'reading' it for live control remains expert tacit knowledge.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen for a consumer/hobbyist tool; note a research robotic tap-hole machine (MIRS) exists for industrial furnaces, but nothing app-market and nothing for reading slag as a craft judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: these slags encapsulate chemical and mineralogical signatures of the raw materials, furnace conditions, and technological practices employed by ancient metallurgists.

concepts.name: Ore roasting / calcination endpoint
concepts.open_problem: Knowing when an ore is adequately roasted/calcined, i.e. when enough sulfur/arsenic has been driven off without over- or under-roasting, is traditionally judged by fumes, color, and smell at the kiln; sources describe the purpose but not a quantified endpoint, leaving the completion call to operator experience.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: The object of calcining or roasting certain ores before treatment is to dissipate sulfur or sulfides of arsenic, antimony, lead, etc., which are inimical to treatment.

concepts.name: Gold panning: reading the pan
concepts.open_problem: Distinguishing real gold from pyrite/mica and spotting fine 'colour' against black sand in the pan by hue, luster, and heft is a learned visual judgment; also reading iron-staining and soil/rock changes in the field to find gold-bearing ground.
concepts.app_market_check: shipping apps exist but for a DIFFERENT task: prospecting apps (Where to Find Gold, Digger's Map, Gold Maps, MineCache) are location/map databases, and 'Gold Detector App' camera mode is a gimmick beep, not real in-pan gold-vs-pyrite recognition; the actual reading-the-pan judgment appears unserved
concepts.verbatim_quote: Real gold is bright yellow (even when wet); pyrite is brassy/greenish, which helps distinguish it from fool's gold.

concepts.name: Fire-assay cupellation judgment
concepts.open_problem: Fire assay (fusion -> lead button -> cupellation -> weighing the prill) depends on the assayer balancing flux/temperature/atmosphere by experience so the precious-metal bead is recovered cleanly; accuracy is explicitly attributed to staff skill rather than to a fully automated decision procedure.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (a lab service, not a consumer app; no shipping product that performs/guides the cupellation judgment)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The key to an accurate assay is the skill and experience of the staff who are able to balance all the factors which may contribute to any variations.

concepts.name: Reading kiln temperature by glow color (pre-cone judgment)
concepts.open_problem: Skilled firers historically judged kiln heat purely by the color of light through peep/bung holes (red->yellow->white); this perceptual mapping of incandescent color to maturation state is tacit, lighting-dependent and still used as a backup when instruments fail.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (AI kiln work targets automated temp control/kiln-packing, not visual color-reading by a human; e.g. Aberystwyth/Parkinson-Spencer kiln-packing ML, generic 'AI-driven kiln' temp control)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Skilled kiln tradespeople would have to judge the heat by the color of the light emanating from holes in the kiln called bung holes (referred to as peep holes in the USA for obvious reasons). As the temperature in the kiln rose, the color would move from red to yellow to white.

concepts.name: Reading pyrometric cone bend as 'heat work' not temperature
concepts.open_problem: Cones integrate time+temperature ('heat work') into a physical slump; the firer must interpret the degree/angle of cone bend to know when a glaze/body has truly matured, a judgment temperature instruments alone cannot give.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no shipping consumer app reads cone deformation; firing-chart reference sites only)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Cones measure 'heat work' which is the combined effect of time and temperature, and clay and glazes are formulated to mature when a certain amount of heat work is achieved.

concepts.name: Judging reduction atmosphere by flame and smell
concepts.open_problem: Without an oxygen analyzer, potters judge whether the kiln is in oxygen-stealing reduction by watching the flame at the peep holes and smelling unburned fuel, then adjusting burners/damper - a multisensory real-time judgment of combustion chemistry.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (oxygen probes exist as hardware, but no app replicates the flame/smell judgment)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Reduction is difficult to judge and not everyone can afford an oxygen analyzer in the kiln.

concepts.name: Wood-firing stoking rhythm / ember-bed management (anagama)
concepts.open_problem: Anagama firing requires teams to judge when to stoke from the look of the pots inside, wetness of walls, ember-bed glow and airflow over multi-day firings; stoking rhythm is adjusted by feel to avoid over-stoking, an unquantified embodied skill.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (a USPTO patent for an 'automated wood-fired kiln' exists as hardware, but no consumer app judges stoking rhythm)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Stoking occurs around the clock until a variety of variables are achieved including the way the fired pots look inside the kiln, the temperature reached and sustained, the amount of ash applied, the wetness of the walls and the pots.

concepts.name: Glaze-defect diagnosis preserving visual character (crazing/crawling)
concepts.open_problem: Correcting crazing/shivering/crawling while keeping a glaze's intended look is described as a classic ceramic-chemistry problem; it requires trade-off judgment across expansion, surface tension and application that resists simple automation.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen for the judgment; glaze-calc software (Glazy, digitalfire) assists chemistry but does not decide the aesthetic trade-off
concepts.verbatim_quote: Crazing appears as a network of fine, spidery cracks that can appear immediately after firing or sometime later.

concepts.name: Judging completion of lime/brick burning by flame cues
concepts.open_problem: In traditional clamp/kiln burning of lime, completion of calcination is read from the disappearance of a blue flame at the top - a perceptual end-point judgment over a multi-week burn with no instrument.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: A blue flame at the top disappears indicates completion.

concepts.name: Lime mortar mix/slaking judgment (tacit, locally-tuned)
concepts.open_problem: The 'perfect mix' for a given situation and the slaking-to-application skill were never well quantified and varied by local materials, passed person-to-person; judging slaking readiness and mix character remains experiential and at risk of being lost.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (premixed NHL products like Ecologic/Lancaster Lime Works sold, but no app judges slaking/mix readiness)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Despite its enduring utility over many centuries, lime mortar's effectiveness as a building material has not been well understood; time-honoured practices were based on tradition, folklore and trade knowledge, vindicated by the vast number of old buildings that remain standing.

concepts.name: Judging cob/earthen mix consistency by foot and feel
concepts.open_problem: Cob mix readiness is judged tactilely (feet sensing consistency, hand/rip tests for straw content); because no two soils are alike, judgment develops only from working the wet material, defying fixed recipes.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: Traditionally, mixing was a process to be learned, with judgment developing out of working directly with the wet material, since the nature and requirements of the particular soil being prepared become apparent as mixing proceeds.

concepts.name: Dry-stone stone selection / fitting by eye
concepts.open_problem: A waller must choose each stone's seen face and fit stones without mortar largely by eye and trial-and-error, drawing on familiarity with regional stone; correct selection per position strongly affects wall lifetime but is not reducible to measurement.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (some academic structural-soundness studies exist; no shipping consumer app picks/fits stones)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Selection of the correct stone for every position in the wall makes an enormous difference to the lifetime of the finished product, and a skilled waller will take time making the selection.

concepts.name: Judging compost maturity by smell/color/feel
concepts.open_problem: The 'look, smell and feel' of finished compost (dark/earthy vs sour/ammonia) is the field-level readiness test used by gardeners and operators, but it is explicitly acknowledged as unreliable and gives little information about true degree of maturation versus lab/process indicators.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as a shipping product; an Alibaba product-insights page discusses an 'AI-powered compost readiness detector app' concept and research e-noses exist, but e-noses are stated to lack precision and no consumer app reliably replaces tactile/odor judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: The look, the smell and the feel of the finished product gives an indication of the maturity, though these techniques are not very reliable.

concepts.name: Knowing when a qanat needs cleaning/maintenance (tacit muqanni knowledge)
concepts.open_problem: Qanats need annual de-silting judged and performed by skilled muqanni who enter shafts and even invented tools to gauge water flow and irrigation timing; this body of traditional construction/maintenance knowledge is documented as being lost with no instrumented replacement.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: Knowledge of building qanats and maintaining them is being lost.

concepts.name: Manual scrap-metal identification by spark test
concepts.open_problem: Ferrous/alloy classification by grinding a sample and reading spark color, volume, nature and length against known samples is a fast cheap human-skill end point, but it cannot positively identify a material (chemistry needed) and depends on the operator's trained eye.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as a phone app for a human's spark read; instead AI bypasses the skill via optical-emission-spectrometry ML (arXiv 1903.09415, F1 ~96.9%) and camera sorters (EverSteel ~20+ categories) at the plant level
concepts.verbatim_quote: The important spark characteristics are color, volume, nature of the spark, and length.

concepts.name: Reading aquaculture pond water quality by color/smell
concepts.open_problem: Experienced farmers judge pond health from water color (green shades = productive, clear = unproductive) and smell (sulfur = oxygen-depletion emergency); it is explicitly a subjective human-eye indicator used where no sensing system exists.
concepts.app_market_check: app exists (XpertSea smartphone app; AquaEasy, AquaPulse, HydroNeo AI water-quality/disease platforms) but these lean on sensors/growth models; a 2022 vision-based water-color ID system is research-stage, not the human color/smell judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: For an experienced farmer, water color is a subjective indicator that can represent water quality and can be directly observed by human eyes when no water quality sensing system is built.

concepts.name: Anaerobic digester health read by foaming/scum and operator vigilance
concepts.open_problem: Operators must spot precursors of a digester upset (foaming/scum, VFA rise, alkalinity drift) before catastrophic foaming; pH explicitly does NOT give early warning, so judgment leans on watching scum/foam and acid-alkalinity ratios over time.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as a consumer/commercial app; vendor troubleshooting guides + lab test kits (Aquafix/Digester Doc) dominate rather than an AI app predicting the upset
concepts.verbatim_quote: Most catastrophic foaming episodes don't appear without warning, and vigilant operators can spot several precursors that indicate a major foaming event may be imminent.

concepts.name: Irrigation scheduling by feel-of-soil and crop look
concepts.open_problem: Traditional scheduling squeezes root-zone soil into a ball/ribbon by hand and reads crop appearance to decide when/how much to water; it lacks a scientific basis and tends to over-irrigate, yet experienced farmers can match sensor results - an unquantified embodied skill.
concepts.app_market_check: apps exist for sensor/ET-based scheduling, but tools that replicate the bare-hand feel-of-soil ribbon judgment are not seen; the manual feel method remains a human skill
concepts.verbatim_quote: The feel and appearance method involves taking a soil sample by hand to estimate moisture content based on how the soil ribbons or clumps.

concepts.name: Manual MRF picking / hand identification of mixed waste
concepts.open_problem: Trained human pickers at material recovery facilities visually identify and pull items machines cannot yet distinguish (textiles, hazardous items, specific plastics); this experiential identification is limited by fatigue/boredom and human-factor variability.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as an app; automation is plant-scale robotic/optical sorters that 'gradually replaced' hand sorting rather than aiding the human picker's judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: Automated sorting gradually replaced hand sorting based on manual labor and worker experience because of its precise identification and efficient separation.

concepts.name: Water dowsing / witching to site a well
concepts.open_problem: Locating groundwater by walking with a forked stick or L-rods that 'respond' over water is a persistent folk practice; it is a tacit bodily judgment with no scientific merit per USGS/NGWA, yet still used to site wells.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no credible app; practice is scientifically rejected, so the 'gap' is that the human ritual persists despite no validity)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The National Ground Water Association, in a position statement, "strongly opposes the use of water witches to locate groundwater on the grounds that controlled experimental evidence clearly indicates that the technique is totally without scientific merit".

concepts.name: Pinpointing buried water-main leaks by ear (listening stick)
concepts.open_problem: Leak technicians localize buried-pipe leaks by listening; different pipe materials and leak types make distinct sounds and bigger leaks 'feather out', so accurate pinpointing requires an experienced ear that not all leaks even satisfy (some are inaudible).
concepts.app_market_check: electronic amplified listening sticks/correlators are sold as hardware (Gutermann, HWM, FCS) that augment the ear, but the interpretive skill stays human; no consumer app replaces it
concepts.verbatim_quote: While all water leaks produce sounds, different types of leaks produce different sounds, and you must be experienced to hear leaks.

concepts.name: Indigo fermentation vat readiness by flower/color/smell
concepts.open_problem: A fermentation indigo vat is judged 'ready/working' by a triad of sensory cues - the blue surface 'flower' (foam of trapped indigo), the yellow-green reduced liquor color, and the distinct bacterial-fermentation odor - rather than by instruments; reading these to decide when to dye and when the vat is alive is tacit and bacteria-dependent.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no consumer app judges indigo vat readiness; only recipe blogs and a microbiota study)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The color, the foam, the smell indicate whether the chemistry is working.

concepts.name: Natural dye-bath exhaustion judgment by color
concepts.open_problem: Dyers reuse a bath for successive 'exhaust' batches and must judge by eye when residual color has dropped enough (and that some dyes like catechu barely exhaust) to predict the paler shade the next fiber will take; this remaining-strength estimate by appearance is experiential and material-specific.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no shipping app estimates dye-bath exhaustion; only craft blogs)
concepts.verbatim_quote: After removing the first batch of fiber, a dye bath typically still contains 30-60% of its original color concentration, and eventually the bath becomes exhausted when no more color transfers.

concepts.name: Vegetable-tanning endpoint judged by sight and feel
concepts.open_problem: In traditional veg tanneries, the condition of hides and tan liquors and the completion of tannage are judged by experienced workers through sight and hand-feel (firmness, grain response, even a flex 'creak'), not automated sensors; knowing when leather has fully struck through is an embodied judgment.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (no app judges tanning endpoint; results were craft/retail guides)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Experienced workers in vegetable tanneries can judge the condition of hides and tanning baths by sight and feel, which keeps the process rooted in human expertise instead of automated systems.

concepts.name: Judging yarn twist / balance by hand (plyback feel)
concepts.open_problem: How much twist 'is enough' for a given fiber is decided by hand - via plyback samples, letting a skein dangle to see if it kinks, and even hearing/feeling the fibers slide - a perceptual, fiber-specific judgment that resists explicit rules despite patents for instrument twist-measurement.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (industrial twist-measurement patents exist as hardware; no consumer app judges handspun twist by feel)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Only skill and experience can tell us how much twist is enough for a particular fiber.

concepts.name: Judging felting/fulling completion by firmness not size
concepts.open_problem: Wet-felters decide a piece is done by real-time tactile feedback - firmness, stability, absence of loose fibers via the pinch test - and control the 'shock' to the fibers by hand, rather than by reaching a target dimension; the stop-point is a felt judgment, not a measurement.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (shrinkage 'calculators' exist but only do arithmetic on a measured sample; no app judges fulling completion)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Rather than relying on dimensions alone, stop felting based on firmness and stability, not just dimensions.

concepts.name: Fleece grading/sorting by hand-feel (wool classing)
concepts.open_problem: Traditional wool classers grade and sort fleeces by trained hand-feel and eye - fineness, staple length/strength, crimp - without instruments, separating qualities within a single fleece that only the hand can distinguish; British Wool says it takes ~3 years to qualify.
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (objective-measurement instruments and AI fibre-science research exist, but no consumer app replaces the hand-classer's tactile grading)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Traditional subjective systems for wool classing rely on the trained judgment of experienced classers to assess fiber characteristics through visual inspection, hand feel, and tactile evaluation, without the use of measurement instruments.

concepts.name: Reading the sky / clouds for tomorrow's weather (weather lore)
concepts.open_problem: Folk forecasting reads sky color (red sky rules), cloud type/sequence and movement over time to anticipate weather; the skill is in integrating evolving cues over days, but the underlying nowcasting task is now heavily served by consumer apps.
concepts.app_market_check: app-saturated - consumer AI weather/nowcasting apps ship widely (Rainbow Weather AI nowcasting, Google WeatherNext in Pixel Weather/Search, AccuWeather, Atmo); the practical 'what's the weather' task is covered
concepts.verbatim_quote: Rainbow Weather delivers hyper-accurate minute-by-minute forecasts powered by AI and machine learning, with a unique nowcasting engine that predicts precipitation up to 4 hours in advance.

concepts.name: Cloud-type reading skill (perceptual, ongoing observation)
concepts.open_problem: Predicting weather from clouds is a centuries-old perceptual skill with modest (~60-75%) accuracy that requires sustained observation of cloud change and motion, not single-snapshot ID; the human reading-of-the-sky-over-time is distinct from app point-forecasts, though apps dominate the end goal.
concepts.app_market_check: partly app-covered - cloud/radar apps (e.g. RainViewer) and AI forecasters serve the prediction goal; less so the embodied 'watch the sky evolve' skill itself
concepts.verbatim_quote: Observing cloud types as a means to predict the weather yields an accuracy of 60–75 percent.

concepts.name: Phenological folk indicators for planting/foraging timing
concepts.open_problem: Traditional practice times planting and wild-harvest by biological cues (lilac bloom -> beans, forsythia -> peas, dogwood bloom end -> stop hunting morels); knowing which local indicator predicts the right window is place-specific traditional knowledge tying plant phenology to soil/temperature readiness.
concepts.app_market_check: partial - citizen-science phenology platforms (USA-NPN Nature's Notebook) and agritech microclimate apps (Sencrop) record/forecast phenology, but the folk indicator->action mapping is not packaged as a consumer app
concepts.verbatim_quote: Examples include planting when the spring peepers begin peeping; treating the lawn for crabgrass when the forsythia is blooming; and ending the hunt for morel mushrooms once the dogwoods stop blooming.

concepts.name: Distinguishing edible vs toxic wild mushrooms (spore/smell/substrate)
concepts.open_problem: Safe ID hinges on hard-to-photograph cues - spore-print color, odor, bruising, substrate - because deadly look-alikes grow alongside edibles; this is a high-stakes multisensory judgment, and notably the AI apps that DO ship are unreliable for the toxic-discrimination part.
concepts.app_market_check: app-saturated but UNSAFE - many mushroom-ID apps ship (Picture Mushroom, Mushroom Identificator, iNaturalist) yet top app scored only ~49% and look-alikes to deadly Amanita/Galerina were misidentified >30% of the time; apps exist but do not solve the safety-critical judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: Most AI-based apps can't take into account the factors crucial to identifying a mushroom with confidence, like the mushroom's substrate, bruising features, and smell.

concepts.name: Surfactant/surface-tension gradient steering of floating pigment (suminagashi soap-ink-oil balance)
concepts.open_problem: Tacit real-time judgment of how each ink/soap/oil drop locally lowers surface tension and where the pigment will flee to; the artist must feel the moment-to-moment Marangoni balance to keep concentric rings from collapsing. No closed-form way to pick drop sequence for a target pattern on a real tray.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial + hydro dipping / water transfer printing floats ink on water and transfers it to an object at factory scale, but it uses a PRE-PRINTED PVA film, not live surface-tension manipulation, so the pattern-creation physics is not industrialized
concepts.app_market_check: app (TryEbru, Watermarbling/hydro.dipping on Google Play, Marblizer browser sim) but all simulate digitally, none control a real fluid tray
concepts.verbatim_quote: Soap reduces the surface tension of water, and when added to floating ink, it creates areas of lower surface tension. The ink moves away from these areas towards regions with higher surface tension, causing the ink to spread out and form the flowing, dynamic patterns.
concepts.source: https://suminagashi.com (via WebSearch snippet, suminagashi fluid pattern control query)

concepts.name: Comb/rake stroke as chaotic-advection control (stretching-and-folding the size to a target figure)
concepts.open_problem: Combing actions stretch and fold the size in a chaotic-advection regime; predicting the resulting figure (e.g. bouquet, peacock) from a stroke sequence on a real bath is unsolved tacit skill, because the mapping is sensitive to initial drop placement and is effectively chaotic.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no + chaotic-advection mixing is studied industrially in stirred tanks, but no factory process renders a controlled marbled FIGURE on a liquid surface for product; the figural patterning has no industrial counterpart
concepts.app_market_check: app (Marblizer, TryEbru) simulate combing digitally; none drive a physical comb
concepts.verbatim_quote: The main idea behind Mathematical Marbling is that combing actions in paper marbling can be modeled by closed-form mathematical transformations, meaning you don't need to run a full-blown fluid solver to accurately simulate a marbled pattern.
concepts.source: https://blog.amandaghassaei.com/2022/10/25/digital-marbling/ (via WebSearch snippet, paper marbling machine learning query)

concepts.name: Size (mucilage) viscosity / density tuning so pigments float and spread correctly
concepts.open_problem: Judging by feel when the carrageenan/cornstarch size has the right viscosity and density for the day's temperature/humidity so colors float and open at the desired rate; an empirical, sensory calibration with no instrument-free rule.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial + viscosity/rheology control is ubiquitous in coatings and printing industry, but tuning a marbling SIZE so hand-applied pigments float-and-bloom is craft-specific and not an industrial line process
concepts.app_market_check: none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: In this method the liquid has to be thickened because the colors used are water-based and would otherwise not float.
concepts.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper_marbling (via WebSearch snippet, paper marbling ebru technique query)

concepts.name: Controlled chance: guiding pigment flow while ceding outcome to the fluid
concepts.open_problem: The core tacit judgment of ebru is balancing deliberate manipulation against the fluid's autonomous behavior ('controlled chance'); knowing how much to intervene vs. let the water act is intuition built over years and is not formalized.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no + no industrial process intentionally couples human steering with stochastic fluid behavior to make an aesthetic surface pattern
concepts.app_market_check: app (digital ebru apps) but they remove the real-fluid stochasticity rather than control it
concepts.verbatim_quote: The foundation of Ebru is the concept of "controlled chance." The artist prepares the medium and sets the colors in motion, but the water, the viscosity, and the natural behavior of the pigments all contribute to the final outcome.
concepts.source: https://www.momentslog.com/culture/the-art-of-turkish-ebru-painting-on-water (via WebSearch snippet, ebru unpredictable intuition query)

concepts.name: Predicting/controlling flake shape from a percussion blow (Hertzian-cone propagation)
concepts.open_problem: Anticipating the size and shape of the flake a given blow will detach from a core is a hard, experience-bound prediction; only highly experienced knappers can do it, showing the judgment is tacit and not reducible to a simple rule.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no + industry CUTS brittle silica by diamond sawing (a different, kerf-removal mechanism); no factory deliberately propagates Hertzian-cone conchoidal fractures to detach shaped flakes
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (only YouTube tutorials and in-person workshops; no dedicated knapping simulator app)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Only modern stone knappers with extensive knapping experience proved capable of predicting and controlling the shape of a flake, indicating the significant difficulty of controlling flake shape.
concepts.source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0047248410000722 (via WebSearch snippet, ML flake shape lithic query)

concepts.name: Platform/angle reading for flake initiation (platform-surface interior angle, exterior platform angle)
concepts.open_problem: Selecting and preparing the striking platform and reading its angle so the fracture initiates and runs as intended is a sensory geometric judgment; there is academic work on PSIA/angle but the in-hand reading remains tacit.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no + no industrial process requires reading a natural-stone platform geometry to launch a controlled conchoidal flake
concepts.app_market_check: none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: Controlled knapping experiments on materials like glass or chert demonstrate that conchoidal outcomes can be anticipated through variables such as hammer angle, with lower angles producing larger, sharper flakes.
concepts.source: https://grokipedia.com/page/Conchoidal_fracture (via WebSearch snippet, conchoidal fracture industrial query)

concepts.name: Pressure-flaking force/termination control (feathering vs. hinge/step termination)
concepts.open_problem: Modulating pressure direction/magnitude with an antler or copper tool, and repositioning the biface, to make each flake feather-terminate instead of leaving a hinge/step fracture is fine haptic skill; nearly impossible to specify numerically and learned by hand-feel.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no + no manufacturing process shapes objects by hand-pressure detachment of conchoidal flakes; closest brittle-material industry (glass scoring/sawing) uses unrelated mechanics
concepts.app_market_check: none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: after each flake removal the biface needs to be moved so that the next flake is resting over the slot. If this is not done the flake will often terminate in a small fingernail hinge at the point where it meets the pad.
concepts.source: https://stonetoolsmuseum.com/technique/pressure-flaking/ (via WebSearch snippet, obsidian pressure flaking query)

concepts.name: Virtual-knapping flake prediction from intact core geometry (CGAN)
concepts.open_problem: Closing the gap between fracture-mechanics theory and what a knapper intuits: predicting flake removal (length/width/volume/shape) from only the intact core surface. A proof-of-concept ML model exists but is explicitly preliminary, so the general predictive problem is open.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no + this is a research model of an ancient hand craft; no industrial percussion-fracture shaping line exists to model
concepts.app_market_check: none seen (research code/PoC only, not a consumer app)
concepts.verbatim_quote: A proof of concept framework uses a conditional adversarial neural network (CGAN) capable of predicting flake removals from 3D cores, with the CGAN accurately predicting the length, volume, width, and shape of flake removals using intact core surface information alone.
concepts.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8497608/ (via WebSearch snippet, ML flake shape lithic query)

concepts.name: Flue-pipe voicing by hand (cutup, flueway, toe adjustment for timbre/volume/attack)
