concepts.verbatim_quote: Key factors in determining spoofing intent include whether the market participant's intent was to induce others to trade when they otherwise would not, whether the intent was to affect a price rather than change their position, whether the intent was to create misleading market conditions.

concepts.name: Corporate-action free-text interpretation & elective-event decisioning
concepts.open_problem: ~46% of event data arrives manually as unstructured free-text offering documents with no uniform structure; firms must independently interpret ambiguous/contradictory terms (and for mandatory-with-choice events make a discretionary election) - a manual interpretive task that resists automation precisely because of inconsistent, non-standard source data.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - mirrors industrial contract/spec/RFQ interpretation and document-to-structured-data extraction where ambiguous vendor docs still need human reading
concepts.app_market_check: Proxymity, FTS Software, FIS Securities Processing, Oracle, Infosys BPM (connectivity/lifecycle tooling; interpretation of unstructured terms still manual)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Globally, it is estimated that 46% of event data is published and received manually, driving unnecessary risk and expense to organizations that process Corporate Action events.

concepts.name: Settlement-fail / reconciliation break exception adjudication
concepts.open_problem: ~15% of reconciliations break and require manual review to confirm root cause across confirmation/matching/settlement; lack of standard data drives ~90% of the manual matching effort - the cause-determination on each break is human judgment, not yet ML-resolved.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - directly analogous to manufacturing ERP/inventory reconciliation and logistics exception-handling (manual root-cause on mismatches)
concepts.app_market_check: Duco, SmartStream, FIS, SolveXia, BlackLine, HighRadius (automate matching; breaks still need human investigation)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Exceptions require manual review to confirm their cause, and their volume and nature are a direct reflection of the health of upstream data quality, integration and matching logic.

concepts.name: IPO bookbuilding allocation discretion
concepts.open_problem: Underwriters allocate shares using discretion conditioned on information beyond the bid (relationship, perceived information quality), so two identical bids get different allocations; this allocation judgment is deliberately human/relational and essentially un-automated (and arguably resists automation by design).
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - resembles discretionary procurement/vendor-award and scarce-capacity allocation decisions in industry, but the relational/information-rent element is fairly finance-specific
concepts.app_market_check: none seen - bookbuilding platforms exist for order capture, but the discretionary allocation call itself is human; no AI allocation product surfaced
concepts.verbatim_quote: The hallmark of bookbuilding is that it allows underwriters to condition allocations on information other than the bid, and underwriters use this discretion extensively.

concepts.name: Proxy-voting 'last 10%' contentious-resolution judgment
concepts.open_problem: ~90% of ballot items are routine and policy-automatable, but the 'last 10%' (contested elections, unusual pay plans, contentious shareholder proposals) require case-by-case human judgment linked to policy criteria with documented, reviewable overrides; AI assists research but the contentious call stays manual.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - akin to policy-exception/edge-case adjudication in industrial compliance & standards committees, though the governance-context reasoning is domain-specific
concepts.app_market_check: ISS, Glass Lewis, Diligent; emerging AI proxy-research tools (per Harvard CorpGov 2026) still position humans for the contentious 10%
concepts.verbatim_quote: while most items are straightforward, the "last 10%" require judgment and careful documentation.

concepts.name: ED triage acuity for subjective chief complaints
concepts.open_problem: Triage of subjective complaints (chest pain, dyspnea, undifferentiated pain) relies on nurse intuition/experience and shows poor-to-fair agreement with algorithms (fewer than half of encounters scored the same, high over/under-triage by ML); the subjective-complaint corner is where automation reliably underperforms and bias appears.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - analogous to industrial fault-severity prioritization from noisy/ambiguous sensor signals, but human-symptom subjectivity has weaker industrial parallel
concepts.app_market_check: Epic/Mednition KATE, Korean KTAS ML models, various LLM-triage research; deployed tools exist but underperform on subjective complaints
concepts.verbatim_quote: One study analyzing 21,469 patient encounters found poor to fair interrater reliability between nurse-assigned and algorithm-assigned triage scores, with fewer than half of ED encounters assigned the same score by both.

concepts.name: Clinical handoff / SBAR salience-selection (what to hand off)
concepts.open_problem: Even with SBAR structure, the human judgment of WHICH information is important enough to transmit (differences in perception of salience) drives omission errors; ~80% of serious errors involve handoff miscommunication and the salience-selection step is essentially un-automated.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - directly mirrors industrial shift-handover/turnover logs in nuclear, aviation, and process plants where what-to-pass-on judgment causes incidents
concepts.app_market_check: none seen as AI - SBAR templates, EHR I-PASS/handoff modules are structured forms, not AI salience selection; no product judging clinical importance surfaced
concepts.verbatim_quote: With each handoff, loss of information and miscommunication is expected due to a large amount of information, high frequency of exchange, and differences in perception of what is important and worth mentioning.

concepts.name: Diagnostic test-ordering stewardship reasoning (right test, right patient)
concepts.open_problem: Current stewardship works mainly via blunt CPOE nudges/hard-stops/education because clinicians have low knowledge of test characteristics; the patient-specific reasoning of which test fits which patient at which time is still human and only crudely supported - nudges work only in low-knowledge/weak-opinion scenarios, not nuanced cases.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - analogous to industrial predictive-maintenance test/inspection selection (which diagnostic to run on which asset when) - partly tooled but selection judgment remains expert-driven
concepts.app_market_check: EHR CPOE alerts/hard-stops (Epic/Cerner), order-set tools; effective products are rule/nudge-based, not AI reasoning about test appropriateness per patient
concepts.verbatim_quote: Hospitalists often are busy, making a host of decisions simultaneously, have a low knowledge of test characteristics (e.g., sensitivity or specificity), and may be unsure of which test to use.

concepts.name: Hospital/ICU discharge-readiness determination
concepts.open_problem: Discharge readiness is commonly decided on mainly subjective physician evaluation with criteria interpreted differently across providers and no established guidelines/ADT policies; ML readiness-prediction exists in research but practice remains subjective, with CDS uptake low or over-relied-upon.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - resembles industrial 'return-to-service / release-from-maintenance' readiness sign-off decisions, though patient/family/social factors weaken the parallel
concepts.app_market_check: research ML discharge-readiness predictors (e.g., patient-flow models); little deployed product, decision stays clinician-subjective
concepts.verbatim_quote: Hospital discharge decisions are now made by physicians based on mainly subjective evaluations of patients' discharge status.

concepts.name: Particle-accelerator online beam tuning by expert operators
concepts.open_problem: Online tuning across huge parameter spaces with sensitive, coupled beam responses is still done mostly by hand between shifts; operators make structure-aware educated guesses that RL/BO optimizers lack, so reproducibility and optimality remain unsolved.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - RL/Bayesian-optimization 'autonomous accelerator' research exists (SLAC, DESY) but is not the production default; manual knob-turning persists
concepts.app_market_check: No commercial product; research codes only (Xopt, Badger/Ocelot, KEK ML injector work) used in-house at national labs
concepts.verbatim_quote: Despite efforts to automate beam tuning, the tuning of particle accelerators is to this day often done manually by experienced human operators.

concepts.name: Cryo-EM grid-square selection during screening
concepts.open_problem: Operator manually scans low-mag grid overview and picks which squares (good ice vs thick/broken) to image at high mag; slow, imprecise, squares overlooked under time pressure, and 'good' is empirical/iterative judgment.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - SmartScope, Smart Leginon, XCryoNet, attention-guided QA automate square scoring, but adoption is uneven and operators still override/curate
concepts.app_market_check: SmartScope (open source), Smart Leginon, Thermo Fisher EPU automation; academic XCryoNet - tooling exists but not a settled commercial standard
concepts.verbatim_quote: A microscope operator would scan the grid for promising squares to further image at higher magnifications, though this process can be slow and imprecise since the operator must manually closely examine squares and squares can be overlooked in the interest of time.

concepts.name: Electron-microscope astigmatism correction at high magnification
concepts.open_problem: At high mag there is no substitute for human eye-hand coordination on stigmator/alignment knobs; auto-stigmation exists but fails in the hardest regime, and perception of beam roundness/translational motion varies operator-to-operator.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - automatic alignment/astigmatism patents and built-in auto-stig on modern SEM/TEM, but explicitly inadequate at high magnification
concepts.app_market_check: Vendor auto-functions (Thermo Fisher, JEOL, Hitachi built-in auto-stigmation); no third-party product for the high-mag manual regime
concepts.verbatim_quote: While many SEMs are now equipped with automated astigmatism correction, there are situations, particularly at high magnification, where there is no substitute for eye-hand coordination to make this important correction.

concepts.name: LC-MS / MRM peak-picking manual curation
concepts.open_problem: Core peak-picking algorithms remain imperfect (poor separation, noise, baseline, peak shape) so every assignment needs manual inspection; not feasible at hundreds-thousands of metabolites, and batch manual-QC tooling is weak.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - deep-learning peak curation (e.g. NeatMS) and MRMPro emerging in literature, but labs still staff dedicated manual-inspection teams
concepts.app_market_check: XCMS, MZmine, Skyline (manual integration); MRMPro web tool; DL curation mostly research - no dominant automated commercial curator
concepts.verbatim_quote: Despite various software solutions and advanced algorithms are available for MRM data analysis, the manual inspection process still remains a time-consuming and labor-intensive task.

concepts.name: Telescope real-time project-switching / weather-band decision
concepts.open_problem: Static queue optimization is automated, but judging when to switch projects as conditions change (and reacting to ToO triggers within weather bands) is left to scheduling staff / observers in real time.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - automated schedulers (AstroQ, LCO network, Gemini queue) handle planning and ToO override logic, but live condition-based switching is human-supervised
concepts.app_market_check: AstroQ, ACP/Scheduler, LCO scheduler, observatory in-house queue tools - planning automated, live override mostly manual
concepts.verbatim_quote: Judging when to switch projects based on changing conditions is left to the telescope scheduling staff and observing team to decide.

concepts.name: Sequencing-run QC interpretation & rerun-eligibility judgment
concepts.open_problem: FastQC-style flags only output Warn/Fail; the human must decide whether a run truly failed for THIS sample/application and whether a rerun is warranted - in-context interpretation, not just metric thresholds, is unautomated.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - QC metric tools (FastQC, MultiQC) compute flags but explicitly punt the contextual pass/fail+rerun decision to the researcher/core staff
concepts.app_market_check: FastQC, MultiQC, instrument vendor QC dashboards report metrics; no product makes the contextual rerun/accept call
concepts.verbatim_quote: When quality control flags indicate "Warn" or "Fail" results, researchers must stop and consider what those results mean in the context of the particular sample and sequencing type used.

concepts.name: Contract redlining / fallback-position judgment
concepts.open_problem: AI flags non-standard clauses and drafts redlines, but choosing the actual fallback/escalation position requires embedded knowledge of the company's risk tolerance, negotiation strategy, relationship history and commercial priorities that tools cannot access.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - many AI review tools surface issues and suggest edits, but the strategic redline decision stays with the lawyer; 'playbook' is the human framework
concepts.app_market_check: Spellbook, Legartis, Luminance, LegalOnTech, Juro, ContractSafe - saturated for issue-spotting/first-pass redlines, not for fallback strategy
concepts.verbatim_quote: Redlining requires deep contextual understanding of your company's risk tolerance, negotiation strategy, fallback clauses, and commercial priorities, and general purpose tools like ChatGPT lack this embedded knowledge and cannot reliably replace a lawyer's judgment.

concepts.name: Regulatory benefit-risk narrative synthesis (FDA/EMA submissions)
concepts.open_problem: AI drafts ~40% (routine tables/boilerplate); the high-judgment benefit-risk story, integrated safety synthesis and cross-module justification - plus catching when AI output is simply wrong - stays with seasoned regulatory writers.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - LLM drafting tools for IND/CTA/510(k) automate routine sections, but interpretive risk-benefit synthesis is explicitly human-controlled
concepts.app_market_check: IntuitionLabs IND/CTA drafting, generic LLMs, CRO medical-writing services - automate routine drafting, not the synthesis judgment
concepts.verbatim_quote: Medical writers handle high-judgment sections such as benefit-risk assessments, integrated analyses, and complex safety issues.

concepts.name: Sanctions-hit adjudication on ambiguous / transliterated names
concepts.open_problem: Fuzzy matchers flood analysts with partial/ambiguous hits driven by transliteration, name reversal, phonetics and cultural variation; the true-match vs false-positive call requires human cultural/linguistic judgment and identity verification.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - entity-resolution/AI matching (Quantifind, Senzing, OpenSanctions) reduces noise, but ambiguous-hit final adjudication remains manual and training-intensive
concepts.app_market_check: Quantifind, Senzing, OpenSanctions, sanctions.io, Descartes, Lenzo - heavy on matching/scoring; the ambiguous-case decision is still analyst-driven
concepts.verbatim_quote: Identity verification, confirming your customer isn't the sanctioned person, requires human judgment on ambiguous cases.

concepts.name: Subjective intent/foul disciplinary judgment for referees
concepts.open_problem: AI handles objective calls (offside, line, ball-tracking) but determining intentionality of a foul and the appropriate disciplinary sanction remains a manual subjective judgment; VAR has not eliminated controversial decisions and no tool decides intent.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - objective tracking (Hawk-Eye, semi-automated offside) is industrialized but the intent/disciplinary layer is not
concepts.app_market_check: Hawk-Eye, FIFA semi-automated offside, VAR exist for objective calls; no product adjudicates intent/sanction
concepts.verbatim_quote: foul-play situations require subjective evaluations to determine the intentionality of the offence and the disciplinary sanction for the offending player

concepts.name: Youth talent identification / projection beyond the scout's eye
concepts.open_problem: Forecasting which youth athletes will succeed is still mostly subjective expert judgment with poor inter-scout agreement and heavy maturation/relative-age bias; no reliable model decomposes the holistic projection.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - pro analytics firms model in-game performance metrics, not future-potential projection of immature youth athletes
concepts.app_market_check: none seen for projection; profiling tools (e.g. academy athlete-profiling tools) capture data but the success forecast stays human
concepts.verbatim_quote: there is poor inter-coach agreement in the identification of talented athletes

concepts.name: Individualized daily-readiness load adjustment / periodization
concepts.open_problem: Training load and periodization still rely on subjective RPE/empirical experience; standardized %1RM and linear models fail to respond to an athlete's daily readiness, leaving the day-to-day adjustment a coach judgment call.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - wearable readiness scores (HRV) exist but the prescription adjustment decision is still manual; early RL research only
concepts.app_market_check: Whoop/Oura/Catapult give readiness signals; no autonomous load-prescriber; one DRL paper is research-stage only
concepts.verbatim_quote: Traditional approaches to training load management predominantly rely on subjective assessments, empirical experience, and standardized protocols

concepts.name: Out-of-plane movement-fault diagnosis from single-camera video
concepts.open_problem: Markerless pose estimation works for single-plane movement but misses 3D compensations; aberrant-movement diagnosis is still largely subjective visual assessment by coaches/physios needing activity-specific multi-camera models that don't exist for most settings.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - markerless pose estimation (OpenPose-class, commercial apps) is maturing but accuracy/3D limits keep diagnosis human
concepts.app_market_check: Sports apps using pose estimation exist (e.g. consumer running-form apps); diagnostic interpretation still expert-driven
concepts.verbatim_quote: movement assessment decisions are still largely made through subjective visual assessment

concepts.name: Supply-chain exception resolution (MRP/PO exceptions)
concepts.open_problem: MRP runs produce thousands of exceptions; planners review, consolidate in spreadsheets, email suppliers and chase by phone, consuming most of the week - the prioritization and resolution judgment is manual.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - this is the classic alert/exception-queue problem; agentic-AI vendors are actively targeting it but adoption is early
concepts.app_market_check: TraceLink, project44, GAINS, autonomous-agent startups market exception tools; most mid-market still manual
concepts.verbatim_quote: the exception resolution process is very tedious and often consumes most of the planner's week

concepts.name: Long-tail / intermittent-demand SKU forecasting
concepts.open_problem: 95%+ of SKUs have intermittent demand with many zero periods; classic and Croston-based models can't reliably set safety stock, so planners make manual overrides and the mix stays wrong (over/understocked).
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - probabilistic demand-sensing is a well-funded vendor space, but accuracy on the deep tail remains an open hard problem
concepts.app_market_check: ToolsGroup, Blue Yonder, o9, ToolsGroup white-papers; tail accuracy still weak despite products
concepts.verbatim_quote: it is very difficult to predict when the next demand will occur and how big it will be

concepts.name: Returns disposition decision for ambiguous/complex categories
concepts.open_problem: Workers still open boxes, inspect for damage, verify serials and make subjective next-destination calls; automated visual grading is emerging but final disposition for complex items (e.g. electronics) stays manual.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - rules+AI grading and automated visual inspection exist for Grade A/B, but edge-case disposition is human
concepts.app_market_check: Loop Returns, ReturnLogic, Optoro-style platforms grade returns; complex disposition still human-inspected
concepts.verbatim_quote: Manual returns processing requires workers to open boxes, inspect items for damage, verify serial numbers, and make subjective decisions about the item's next destination

concepts.name: Ambiguous receiving discrepancy / damaged-goods exception calls
concepts.open_problem: At inbound receiving, deciding accept/reject/quarantine on damaged or PO-mismatched goods is a worker judgment call documented with photos and notes; WMS reduces but cannot eliminate these discrepancy decisions.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - WMS records and flags discrepancies but does not adjudicate the ambiguous accept/quarantine decision
concepts.app_market_check: WMS (SAP, etc.) log and quarantine; no product makes the judgment call - guidance is checklists and two-person checks
concepts.verbatim_quote: While a Warehouse Management System significantly reduces inventory discrepancies, it cannot eliminate them entirely

concepts.name: Open-ended rubric calibration & confidence-gated routing
concepts.open_problem: Even with LLM-as-judge, pedagogically rich/ambiguous open responses must be routed to humans; calibrating rubrics against expert standards and deciding the confidence threshold for human escalation is still a manual judgment loop.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - confidence-gated routing in industrial QA/manufacturing inspection is mature, directly transferable
concepts.app_market_check: Turnitin/Gradescope AI-assist, many LLM-judge frameworks (RATAS, etc.) seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: When AI systems were delivered with stricter confidence filtering settings to achieve human-level accuracy, roughly 70% of items still needed to be graded by humans.

concepts.name: Student misconception diagnosis (definition/granularity)
concepts.open_problem: Identifying the specific misconception behind a wrong answer remains ad-hoc; misconceptions overlap and are ambiguous to define, so discovery still needs experts inspecting student-work traces or interviews.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - akin to root-cause/fault classification in diagnostics, but the 'fault taxonomy' here is ill-defined and human-curated
concepts.app_market_check: research prototypes only (semi-auto discovery via code embeddings, MCTS distractor gen); no dominant commercial product seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: A misconception is ambiguous to define, with the granularity and scope of a misconception often making detection an ad-hoc and intuition-driven process.

concepts.name: Viva voce / oral-exam authenticity & competence judgment
concepts.open_problem: Live oral defense to judge originality AND grasp simultaneously is inherently subjective and unscalable; examiners adapt follow-up questions in real time and weigh communication/ethical judgment - not automated, only simulated for practice.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - real-time adaptive interrogation with a competence verdict has no clean industrial sensor/control analog
concepts.app_market_check: LLM viva 'simulators' exist (arXiv 2511.05530, Eklavvya online viva) but for practice/scale, not replacing the human verdict
concepts.verbatim_quote: Two problems with the use of viva voce examinations is their lack of scalability and their subjectivity.

concepts.name: AI-authorship / plagiarism authenticity nuance adjudication
concepts.open_problem: Detectors produce contested false positives (esp. non-native writers); the actual academic-integrity decision requires a human to weigh context, stylistic evidence, and appeals - the judgment call is irreducibly manual.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - similar to fraud-flag adjudication in finance (model flags, human adjudicates), transferable workflow
concepts.app_market_check: Turnitin, GPTZero, CopyLeaks all exist as detectors; adjudication layer is human/policy, not productized
concepts.verbatim_quote: Research from Stanford University found that AI detectors misclassified over 61% of essays written by non-native English speakers as AI-generated, compared to near-perfect accuracy on native speaker essays.

concepts.name: Curriculum sequencing / knowledge-dependency mapping
concepts.open_problem: Mapping prerequisite knowledge dependencies and sequencing concepts (concrete-before-abstract, cognitive-load pacing) is a consensus-building expert task; adaptive engines reorder existing items but the dependency graph + progression design is human.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - like dependency/DAG scheduling in project planning, but pedagogical ordering needs domain semantics
concepts.app_market_check: Knewton/Alta adaptive sequencing (item-level), ALEKS; but knowledge-graph/progression authoring still expert-driven
concepts.verbatim_quote: Developing learning progressions should be a collaborative effort among teachers, curriculum developers, and subject matter experts.

concepts.name: Rail dispatching real-time conflict resolution
concepts.open_problem: Resolving train conflicts (re-ordering, re-routing, knock-on delay tradeoffs across territory boundaries) is still almost entirely manual; dispatchers rely on experience and limited inputs, often ignoring network-wide knock-on effects.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - job-shop/real-time scheduling under disruption is well studied industrially; deep-RL approaches emerging but not deployed as arbiter
concepts.app_market_check: AAR notes decision-support/alerts exist; conflict resolution itself remains under human control, no autonomous product seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: The task of conflict resolution in railway dispatching is still completely under manual control of human dispatchers, though visualization tools and other systems exist to assist them.

concepts.name: Grid black-start / restoration sequencing operator judgment
concepts.open_problem: Selecting among black-start plans, island formation order, and frequency/phase-matched re-synchronization under cold-load-pickup uncertainty is a high-stakes, deliberate human decision; plans are pre-built but live execution choices are operator judgment.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - constrained sequencing/optimization analog exists (and is researched), but safety-criticality keeps a human arbiter
concepts.app_market_check: Eaton CYME restoration module, S&C EdgeRestore (distribution auto-switching) exist; transmission black-start sequencing largely plan+operator
concepts.verbatim_quote: Grid operators have to be very deliberate about how many customers they restore service to at a time.

concepts.name: Traffic-signal retiming engineering
concepts.open_problem: Retiming intersections is staff-hour heavy (20-25 hrs/intersection) and gated by engineer scarcity; while data collection is being automated, the timing-plan engineering judgment per corridor is still manual and under-staffed.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - control-loop/optimization analog (adaptive signal control) exists but most signals run fixed plans retimed by hand
concepts.app_market_check: Rhythm code|GREEN, Parsons Intelligent Intersections, adaptive systems exist but cover a minority of intersections
concepts.verbatim_quote: A signal retiming program should take around 20 to 25 staff hours per intersection.

concepts.name: Water-network leak pinpointing (acoustic field judgment)
concepts.open_problem: Final pinpointing of a leak by acoustic listening is skill-dependent, non-systematic, and degrades with operator fatigue/inexperience; the interpretive 'is that the leak' call in the field is still human.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - vibration/acoustic condition-monitoring & fault localization is mature industrially, transferable
concepts.app_market_check: AI acoustic detection w/ cloud + mobile guidance reported (>90% acc), noise loggers commercial; but field pinpoint judgment still operator-led
concepts.verbatim_quote: The acoustic listening method manually conducted by waterworks operators during routine leak pinpointing tasks is typically labor-intensive, skill-dependent, non-systematic, and sometimes imprecise due to fatigue and inexperience of newly trained staff.

concepts.name: Event-based surveillance signal triage (manual cluster verification)
concepts.open_problem: Epidemiologists manually read large volumes of unstructured signals (media, rumors, reports) and decide which tiny fraction to escalate/verify as real events; the cluster triage step is still primarily manual and only ~0.3% of raw signals get escalated, demanding human judgment on what 'unusual' means in local context.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial + general alert-fatigue/anomaly-triage exists in SOC/SIEM cybersecurity and NLP de-duplication, but health-event semantics & verification judgment are domain-specific
concepts.app_market_check: WHO EIOS and HealthMap/EpiCore aggregate signals; research prototype EventEpi (NLP framework) exists but is not a deployed product; verification/triage decision largely manual
concepts.verbatim_quote: amongst 43,631 raw signals detected, 138 (0.3%) were escalated; 63 (46%) of those were verified as events

concepts.name: Foodborne outbreak hypothesis generation from trawling interviews
concepts.open_problem: After a cluster is flagged, epidemiologists conduct open-ended 'trawling' interviews asking sick people about every food/restaurant/event, then subjectively generate a hypothesis for the likely vehicle; this is labour-intensive, time-consuming, error-prone, and most outbreak vehicles remain unidentified. The judgment of forming the right hypothesis from sparse, noisy recall is the gap.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial + consumer-purchase-data mining is an emerging alternative analog, but free-text recall reconciliation and abductive hypothesis-forming has weak direct industrial equivalent
concepts.app_market_check: PulseNet does genomic clustering (the upstream detection step), but no widely-deployed product for the interview-to-hypothesis judgment; consumer-purchase-data approaches are research-stage
concepts.verbatim_quote: These procedures are labour-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to error.

concepts.name: Wilderness SAR probability-of-area (POA) consensus estimation
concepts.open_problem: Ground search planners assign subjective probabilities to map segments (where is the lost person) via a 'Mattson Consensus' averaging exercise; these human probability judgments are demonstrably affected by cognitive biases (e.g., anchoring) that the consensus method does not fully correct, and there is no standard algorithm replacing the expert judgment call for terrestrial searches.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial + Bayesian search theory is mature for maritime (SAROPS) and expert-elicitation methods exist, but land-search lost-person-behavior priors remain a manual consensus judgment
concepts.app_market_check: SARTopo/CalTopo used for mapping; ISRID dataset informs priors; maritime SAROPS/SARPlan automate at sea, but land POA estimation is still a manual consensus exercise
concepts.verbatim_quote: the consensus method of developing a search plan does not appear to adequately address one particular bias

concepts.name: Disaster relief supply pre-positioning / staging decisions
concepts.open_problem: Incident commanders and emergency managers decide what relief resources to pre-position where and when before/at the start of an event, and how to deploy the flood of incoming aid; in practice this is driven by the IC's plan, experience, and judgment under deep uncertainty rather than a standard optimizer integrated into the field workflow.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes + strong analog to commercial supply-chain pre-positioning/inventory placement and stochastic facility location optimization
concepts.app_market_check: Rich academic literature (multi-stage stochastic programming, location-allocation models) but little evidence of a field-deployed product; decision remains plan/experience-driven in ICS
concepts.verbatim_quote: As Incident Commander, one of the most daunting tasks ahead is the management of incoming resources and deployment in accordance with YOUR plan.

concepts.name: Vaccine cold-chain temperature-excursion disposition judgment
concepts.open_problem: When a temperature excursion occurs, frontline staff must judge whether vaccines are still usable or damaged (freezing can be as harmful as heat); a large majority report they lack the tools to make this call, leaving a manual, error-prone disposition decision at the point of care.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes + direct analog to pharma/biologics cold-chain stability-budget (MKT) excursion management in commercial logistics
concepts.app_market_check: Monitoring hardware/loggers exist (SenseAnywhere, Berlinger, Controlant) and WHO stability-budget tools, but the use/discard judgment support at the clinic is largely manual
concepts.verbatim_quote: 91% of staff believed that they did not have the necessary tools to detect if a vaccine had been damaged by a temperature excursion

concepts.name: Wastewater surveillance signal interpretation
concepts.open_problem: Translating raw viral RNA/DNA concentrations in sewage into actionable public-health meaning (rising? real? what population? what action?) requires expert judgment because shedding rates/timing vary by pathogen and sewersheds don't map to political boundaries; officials find it very difficult to interpret for decision-making.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial + general environmental-sensor time-series anomaly detection and normalization is a known analog, but pathogen-specific shedding and burden inference is domain-specific
concepts.app_market_check: Biobot, WastewaterSCAN, Verily, CDC NWSS provide dashboards/normalized data; simple ML and Bayesian methods are research-stage; the burden/action interpretation is still expert-led
concepts.verbatim_quote: it is very difficult for public health officials to interpret and use viral RNA or DNA concentrations in wastewater for decision-making purposes

concepts.name: Dynamic ambulance relocation between calls
concepts.open_problem: Dispatchers/supervisors decide where to move idle ambulances to wait for the next emergency and which unit to send; in real operations relocation is commonly changed manually based on experience and professional judgment despite a large optimization literature, with persistent gaps in patient-outcome-aware and rural deployment.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes + strong analog to rideshare/fleet repositioning and on-demand logistics dispatch optimization
concepts.app_market_check: CAD vendors and analytics exist (e.g., MARVLIS/Bradshaw, ESO, RapidDeploy) plus approximate dynamic programming research; many agencies still relocate by experience
concepts.verbatim_quote: the commonly used method to recover from disturbances in practice is to change deployment manually based on experiences and professional judgements

concepts.name: 911 / emergency call risk triage and prioritization
concepts.open_problem: Call-takers assess urgency and decide unit response from speech, noise, and context; the field has explicitly settled on a human-in-the-loop model where empathy/intuition stay with humans, so the judgment-heavy triage call is deliberately only AI-assisted, not automated.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes + direct analog to contact-center NLP intent/priority routing and risk scoring
concepts.app_market_check: Many vendors: Prepared911, Carbyne, RapidSOS, Corti, plus NLP research on police calls-for-service; saturated assistive layer
concepts.verbatim_quote: Machine Learning can support the professional judgement of experienced human operators with a precise, low-latency forecast of call risk

concepts.name: 911 call empathy/judgment triage on degraded audio
concepts.open_problem: Deciding acuity and whether to involve law enforcement when callers are panicked, accented, traumatized, or in noisy environments — the empathy/intuition layer where AI fails and a human must weigh ambiguous spoken cues in real time.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial — call-center voice IVR/sentiment exists, but emergency degraded-audio + judgment-under-trauma is far harder than commercial telephony
concepts.app_market_check: BlueSentry (Avairy), Hexagon/RapidDeploy, Carbyne, Aurelian, Prepared911 — vendors target non-emergency overflow, not the judgment core
concepts.verbatim_quote: The technology often struggles with background noise, accents, trauma responses, or speech related to medical conditions.

concepts.name: EMD acuity determination / over-undertriage tuning
concepts.open_problem: Closing the gap between dispatch-assigned priority and on-scene reality; Medical Priority Dispatch protocols overtriage at ~62% (target 25-35%) — a structured-protocol-plus-human-judgment task to right-size ambulance acuity that resists pure automation.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial — predictive triage exists in clinical ED settings, but pre-arrival phone-only acuity with no patient exam is a distinct unsolved gap
concepts.app_market_check: Priority Dispatch (ProQA/MPDS) is the dominant protocol-card system; largely deterministic, not ML; nurse-triage add-ons exist but no ML acuity engine widely deployed
concepts.verbatim_quote: Overtriage occurs when patients are triaged on-scene by EMS staff as lower acuity but were dispatched as high priority (P1).

concepts.name: SAR mission tasking & search-segment prioritization
concepts.open_problem: The IC's minute-by-minute call of which segment to assign which arriving resource — translating Lost Person Behavior probability into segment tasking and dynamic re-tasking remains manual map-work and human judgment, not optimization.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no — field logistics dispatch optimizers exist commercially but probabilistic-area lost-person tasking under terrain/weather/clue uncertainty has no real industrial twin
concepts.app_market_check: CalTopo / SARTopo dominate; provide mapping, segments, LPB layers and 'probability-based heat mapping features being developed' — but resource-to-segment tasking is still the manager's manual decision
concepts.verbatim_quote: The SAR Incident Commander is responsible for the coordination and control of all incident activities and the associated minute-by-minute decisions, and is accountable for the overall success or failure of the mission.

concepts.name: Wildfire incident-command resource staging decisions
concepts.open_problem: Recognition-primed IC choices on where to stage and pre-position crews/engines under fast-changing fire behavior — doctrine explicitly demands judgment, not procedure, leaving the staging/mobilization-center allocation call essentially un-automated.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial — supply-chain pre-positioning/inventory staging optimizers exist, but fire's recognition-primed, life-safety, rapidly-evolving front makes them a weak analog
concepts.app_market_check: Technosylva (Wildfire Analyst/fiResponse), IBM EIS, Intterra, Tablet Command — fire-spread prediction and CAD exist; the staging-decision layer remains the IC's call
concepts.verbatim_quote: Fire operations doctrine does not consist of procedures to be applied to specific situations so much as it sets forth general guidance that requires judgment.

concepts.name: Disaster preliminary damage assessment field verification
concepts.open_problem: Human ground-truth validation of damage severity that feeds Presidential-declaration eligibility — even with imagery/Survey123, field assessors must adjudicate damage categories per-structure, a judgment + verification gap remote sensing alone can't close.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial — insurance claims damage adjudication is close, but FEMA's declaration-threshold standardized categorization is a niche public-sector decision
concepts.app_market_check: FEMA FACT System + Esri ArcGIS Survey123 PDA templates (data collection); no ML severity-adjudication product seen for the decision itself
concepts.verbatim_quote: Visual interpretation is very important as well as the experience of the map provider in order to contain as much as possible the limitations of the automatic processing.

concepts.name: Outbreak rumor/signal verification (true-vs-noise triage)
concepts.open_problem: Epidemiologists manually verifying whether an unofficial outbreak rumor is real before triggering costly response — true events verified in ~2.7 days, false rumors ~9.3 days; the curation/verification judgment is human and slow.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial — fraud/misinformation detection pipelines are analogous for the text-signal step, but epidemiological consequence-weighting of an unverified threat is domain-specific
concepts.app_market_check: WHO EIOS, ProMED, HealthMap, EpiCore/Ending Pandemics, BlueDot, Metabiota — aggregation/detection exist; verification still relies on 'human input ... for data curation and signal verification'
concepts.verbatim_quote: Human input plays a crucial role for data curation and signal verification.

concepts.name: Syndromic-surveillance alarm adjudication (Alert/Monitor/No-action)
concepts.open_problem: After low-threshold statistical alarms fire (high false-positive rates), an epidemiologist must do a second-stage manual review and assign Alert/Monitor/No-action — the contextual public-health-significance call is still human.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial — SOC/IT anomaly-alert triage (SIEM tier-2) is a strong structural twin for the false-positive triage problem
concepts.app_market_check: ESSENCE (NSSP/CDC BioSense), EARS, England's RCGP/UKHSA system; one PMC study applies ML to 'refine decision making' — so some penetration, but adjudication is the analyst's
concepts.verbatim_quote: Syndromic surveillance systems have to follow up alarms with a second stage process to determine whether individual alarms are of potential public health importance.

concepts.name: Wastewater signal interpretation -> public-health action
concepts.open_problem: Turning noisy multi-site wastewater pathogen-load data into an actionable 'worsening trend / act now' call — explicitly mixes statistics with expert judgment, and local depts often lack the skills, so the interpretation step is a manual bottleneck.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial — industrial process/sensor anomaly trend detection is analogous, but cross-site normalization + public-health action-triggering is specialized
concepts.app_market_check: Biobot Analytics, Verily (CDC NWSS contract / WastewaterSCAN) provide dashboards & trends; the interpret-and-act decision still needs expert judgment per CDC guidance
concepts.verbatim_quote: Various methods are employed to draw inferences ... from tests of statistical significance to application of expert judgment. However, these analyses require skills that are not always readily available within the jurisdiction or local public health department.

concepts.name: Contact-tracing interview prioritization sequencing
concepts.open_problem: Which contact to interview next given limited tracers — a sequential decision with downstream branching effects (querying B vs C changes future options); currently a heuristic human call, only recently framed as a 'branching bandit' optimization.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes — operations-research scheduling/bandit problems and call-center next-best-action queuing are direct analogs
concepts.app_market_check: Sara Alert, Salesforce Work.com / Contact Tracing, Dimagi CommCare; case-management workflow tools exist but next-contact prioritization optimization is not a shipped product feature
concepts.verbatim_quote: A crucial decision in any contact tracing strategy is which person should a tracer trace next, given a set of contacts.

concepts.name: Risk-based health-inspection targeting
concepts.open_problem: Allocating scarce inspectors by establishment risk — frequency still driven by static risk tiers + inspection history + complaint volume rather than dynamic predictive targeting in most jurisdictions.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes — predictive maintenance / audit-risk-scoring (tax, manufacturing QA) is a direct twin and well developed
concepts.app_market_check: FieldPie, MyFieldAudits, HealthSpace, Accela; mostly checklist/grading workflow; Chicago/Yelp-data predictive-inspection pilots exist (academic), limited production ML
concepts.verbatim_quote: Health inspection frequency depends on several factors reflecting an establishment's risk profile, with high-risk operations typically facing inspections every 6-12 months.

concepts.name: Vaccine cold-chain temperature-excursion disposition call
concepts.open_problem: After an excursion, deciding whether product is still usable vs must be discarded, and re-routing last-mile under supply uncertainty — stability-budget judgment that's partly procedural but still a human disposition decision at the point of delivery.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes — pharma/perishables cold-chain logistics and shelf-life disposition is a mature commercial discipline
concepts.app_market_check: Controlant, Sensitech, Berlinger, Zipline (last-mile); route+excursion decision-support 'two-stage' approaches are research-stage, monitoring is productized
concepts.verbatim_quote: The sustainable last-mile cold chain logistics operations of COVID-19 vaccines is a complex short-term planning problem that faces many practical challenges.
